title: HarborCare POC scoping - quality eval plan
next_steps: Sophie to send POC statement of work and pricing options (hosted vs dedicated)
Miguel to run initial 10k-record benchmark and share latency/cost spreadsheet
Customer to share golden prompts + 200 labeled examples and sample schema
Schedule kickoff for data ingestion next Tue
action_items: Sophie Zhang: send POC SOW, pricing and hosting TCO (due 2026-06-18)
Miguel Ortega: run benchmark on 10k patient messages, produce latency/cost spreadsheet (due 2026-06-19)
Priya Menon: provide golden prompts and 200 annotated examples for QA (due 2026-06-17)
Dana Lee: share SOC2 report and data residency checklist (due 2026-06-18)
Liam O'Connor: share sample API payloads and schema (due 2026-06-17)
summary: Discovery and POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan for a 4-week POC. Covered success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarking plan, latency/cost targets, and detailed quality tests (golden prompts, regression sets, hallucination checks, format checks, and scoring). Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Zhang: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we, we should be able to keep this to about 45 minutes, we have Miguel from infra, and we'll dive into the quality eval plan for the poc.
[00:12] Priya Menon: thanks, Sophie, appreciate it. We wanna make sure the model is safe for clinical note summarization and triage suggestions, so quality is the top success metric.
[00:25] Miguel Ortega: quick logistics, are we still aiming for a 4 week POC? and is this hosted or private? i heard mixed earlier.
[00:34] Maya Singh: yes 4 weeks, ideally private VPC but we're open to hosted if the data residency and KMS meet our reqs.
[00:43] Dana Lee: from privacy side we need SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO, KMS integration and audit logs; if hosted can't store raw PHI beyond 30 days.
[00:55] Sophie Zhang: totally, we can do Private deployment or Dedicated, both support customer-managed KMS and VPC. we'll include SOC2 and iso artifacts in the security pack.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: on throughput, our peak is about 1,200 requests per minute for triage, average message length 120 tokens, but we also have bursts up to 3k RPM during morning.
[01:18] Miguel Ortega: ok useful. For the benchmark we'll size by concurrent workers and batch size; want to confirm target latency SLOs?
[01:26] Priya Menon: 95p latency under 350ms for single-turn generation is preferred, but we can accept a 400-500ms tail if it lowers cost. accuracy for diagnoses suggestions must be very high, hallucination under 1% on critical fields.
[01:40] Evan Brooks: to add clinical context, the output needs structured sections: "assessment", "plan", and any flags for escalation; those formats must be exact or downstream systems break.
[01:50] Sophie Zhang: noted, so success criteria we captured: 1) hallucination rate <1% on critical fields, 2) F1 >0.9 for entity extraction on our annotated set, 3) 95p latency <350-400ms, 4) deterministic format compliance >98% on structured outputs, and 5) cost per 1k tokens within your budget threshold - we'll quantify.
[02:10] Priya Menon: yes that's what we're after.
[02:14] Miguel Ortega: ok let's talk evaluation data: can you share a seed set of golden prompts and about 200 labeled examples for scoring?
[02:22] Priya Menon: we can provide 200 labeled clinical notes plus 30 golden prompts that represent edge cases.
[02:28] Sophie Zhang: perfect - the quality eval plan we propose: baseline run on open model variants, regression tests on historical examples, hallucination checks, structured format tests, and a scoring approach that combines automatic embedding-similarity scoring with human review samples.
[02:43] Liam O'Connor: can you explain embedding similarity scoring?
[02:46] Miguel Ortega: sure, we embed the model outputs and the human reference and use cosine similarity; for entities we compute exact-match and span-F1. for long-form summary we use semantic similarity thresholds rather than BLEU or ROUGE because those don't capture clinical adequacy.
[03:00] Priya Menon: how do you detect hallucinations?
[03:03] Sophie Zhang: good question. we run a heuristic check for unsupported factual claims against the source text, and flag outputs that reference entities not present in the input. we also run a separate citation-safety test for any assertions that should be referenced - we'll label those as high-risk.
[03:18] Evan Brooks: sometimes the model invents medication names or dosages - that's a show-stopper.
[03:22] Miguel Ortega: agreed; for meds/dosage we do entity-level checks and require provenance or exact match to input. hallucination threshold is separately measured for critical fields.
[03:30] Sophie Zhang: on the regression tests: we'll construct a regression suite from 500 historical cases, split into train/validation-like sets: 200 golden, 200 common cases, 100 edge/failure cases. We'll include seeding for adversarial prompts and some obfuscated patient text to ensure robustness.
[03:52] Maya Singh: timeline wise how long to get initial numbers?
[03:56] Miguel Ortega: if we get the annotated set and sample schema by next Wed (2026-06-17) we can run the baseline 10k-run benchmark and return a latency/cost sheet by Fri (2026-06-19).
[04:08] Sophie Zhang: POC phases: week 0 kickoff & data ingestion, week 1 baseline & bench, week 2 tuning & dedicated config (quantization and batching), week 3 regression & human eval, week 4 final report and handoff. that's the typical 4 week flow.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. Can you detail the scoring approach?
[04:30] Sophie Zhang: absolutely. scoring will have multiple components combined into a final quality score:
- Automatic metrics (70% weight):
  - Entity F1 / exact match (30%)
  - Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) for free-text summary (20%)
  - Format compliance (exact header/section matching) (20%)
- Human evaluation (30% weight):
  - Clinical adequacy (15%)
  - Hallucination presence/impact (10%)
  - Usability / downstream integration fit (5%)
We'll compute per-scenario scores and aggregate across the golden set.
[05:10] Priya Menon: what's the acceptance threshold?
[05:13] Sophie Zhang: propose final quality score >= 0.88 with entity F1 >= 0.9 and hallucination rate <1% for critical fields. we're happy to adjust thresholds with you.
[05:25] Dana Lee: on security and logging, we need audit logs of each request, description of key rotation, and proof of data access controls for the POC.
[05:35] Miguel Ortega: noted - Dedicated and Private both support audit logs and customer KMS; we'll include a short doc on retention and access controls.
[05:43] Priya Menon: what about performance tuning - quantization? does it change output quality?
[05:48] Miguel Ortega: quant can introduce small quality deltas; part of the POC tuning phase we'll run quantized variants (q4, q8) and measure quality delta per the scoring plan. we'll also test batching and KV-cache effects for chat-style flows.
[06:02] Sophie Zhang: for benchmarks we'll run two workload profiles: triage (short prompts, high rps) and summarization (longer prompts, higher token generation). target sample sizes: 10k triage messages and 2k summarization cases.
[06:17] Evan Brooks: are you including end-to-end downstream testing? like pushing the generated JSON into our pipeline?
[06:21] Miguel Ortega: yes we'll validate format and ingestibility. we'll also produce a sample CI check that fails the build if format compliance drops below threshold.
[06:30] Maya Singh: what's the expected cost reporting format?
[06:33] Sophie Zhang: we'll share a spreadsheet with per-model per-1k-token cost, plus projected monthly cost at your expected volume and a dedicated reserve estimate if you choose Dedicated.
[06:45] Liam O'Connor: do you have recommended golden prompts templates?
[06:48] Sophie Zhang: yes, we'll share templates for clinical summarization, triage, and escalation prompting. golden prompts should include instruction, context, and desired JSON schema where applicable.
[06:59] Priya Menon: about regression - do you run adversarial perturbations? we have some attack cases we can share.
[07:05] Miguel Ortega: we'll include adversarial checks: spelling errors, truncated context, redaction, obfuscation, and injection patterns. those are added to the failure set.
[07:16] Sophie Zhang: now, hallucination/format checks details:
- Hallucination checks: entity cross-checks, unsupported assertion detection, and external-knowledge claims flagged. We'll run a secondary check that looks for 'fabricated facts' by comparing to input context.
- Format checks: exact-match of JSON keys, presence of required sections, field-level regex for dates/dosages, and downstream schema validation.
[07:48] Evan Brooks: regex for dosages might be tricky, but fine. we can provide examples.
[07:53] Sophie Zhang: scoring approach for hallucinations will be binary at field-level (0/1) and severity-weighted - a hallucinated dosage is high severity, free-text minor misstatements are lower severity.
[08:06] Priya Menon: what's the human eval sample size?
[08:09] Miguel Ortega: propose 100 human-review cases: 60 golden, 30 edge, 10 adversarial. clinicians will label adequacy and hallucination impact.
[08:19] Maya Singh: ok good. will Redwood help recruit clinicians or do we use our own?
[08:23] Sophie Zhang: customers typically provide clinicians for domain knowledge; we can support annotation tooling and a recommended rubric.
[08:32] Liam O'Connor: can you commit to a confidentiality agreement for samples we share?
[08:35] Dana Lee: yes that's critical.
[08:37] Sophie Zhang: absolutely we'll include an NDA annex and treat PII/PHI per the data handling addendum.
[08:45] Priya Menon: what about rollbacks and model variants? if tuned model regresses we need automatic fallback.
[08:52] Miguel Ortega: Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to previous model variant or a lower-cost hosted model. we'll include canary steps in the POC.
[08:59] Sophie Zhang: ok let's be concrete about deliverables for the POC quality eval plan:
1) Baseline report with latency/cost and quality scores on golden set.
2) Regression suite of 500 cases and automated tests.
3) Human evaluation results with clinician annotations.
4) Final scoring dashboard and recommendations (quantization, batching, model choice).
[09:25] Priya Menon: timeline and acceptance again?
[09:28] Sophie Zhang: baseline numbers by 2026-06-19, weekly syncs, final report at end of week 4 (target 2026-07-10). acceptance criteria: quality score >=0.88, F1 >=0.9, hallucination <1% on critical fields, format compliance >98%.
[09:45] Evan Brooks: also want a risk register for any unresolved quality issues.
[09:49] Sophie Zhang: we'll include that in the final report.
[09:52] Liam O'Connor: regarding infra, do you support private on-prem?
[09:55] Miguel Ortega: yes we have an on-prem packaging option for air-gapped deployments, though that's a longer timeline and separate contract. for this POC we'll stick to Private VPC or Dedicated.
[10:06] Priya Menon: ok, about golden prompts - we'll include normal and edge-case prompts, and also a list of blacklisted instructions we never want the model to follow.
[10:14] Sophie Zhang: good idea. blacklist rules will be enforced in the eval harness and we can include hard filters for PII exfiltration.
[10:22] Miguel Ortega: technical notes on benchmarks: we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll run both k8s-based runner and Redwood runtime variant.
[10:36] Maya Singh: what about model quantization levels you test?
[10:39] Miguel Ortega: q4, q8 at minimum, plus a float baseline. we'll show delta in quality and cost.
[10:45] Priya Menon: what about retraining or fine-tuning?
[10:49] Sophie Zhang: for the POC we recommend adapter-style fine-tuning or instruction tuning if needed after baseline. full fine-tuning is possible but needs more time and separate infra.
[11:00] Evan Brooks: can we set up automatic regression runs every commit?
[11:03] Miguel Ortega: yes we'll provide CI hooks that run the regression suite and block merges if quality drops.
[11:10] Sophie Zhang: okay any other questions before we wrap?
[11:12] Dana Lee: please include a data retention plan in the security pack.
[11:16] Sophie Zhang: will do.
[11:19] Priya Menon: please also include examples of the scoring dashboard.
[11:22] Sophie Zhang: yep.
[11:25] Miguel Ortega: i will start the benchmark once we get the sample set.
[11:28] Sophie Zhang: great, i'll follow up with SOW and schedule the kickoff. thanks everyone.
[47:30] End of recording: meeting closed

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings, e.g., "redwood dedicate" for "Redwood Dedicated" or "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k-v cash". Speakers sometimes overlap and proper nouns may be incorrect.
